introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Statistics Paper 2 (0770/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
incertitudes: Q6(i) : sujet imprimé défectueux. La fonction est définie par « x^2 - 2 pour 0 <= x < 2 » et « 4 - x pour 2 <= x <= 4 » avec la période 4 : la borne fermée x = 4 donnerait f(4) = 0, alors que la périodicité impose f(4) = f(0) = -2 (la fonction ne serait pas bien définie). Le corrigé le démontre et retient la définition cohérente (seconde branche sur 2 <= x < 4, donc f(4) = f(0) = -2). Les valeurs demandées en (a), f(19) et f(-43), ne dépendent pas de ce point (19 et -43 ne sont pas congrus à 0 ou 2 modulo 4).
Q6(i)(a) : le second argument est lu « f(-43) » (le chiffre 3 est un peu serré contre la parenthèse sur le scan).
Q6(i)(b) : aucune figure imprimée ; le tracé est à faire par le candidat et il est décrit dans le corrigé (tableau de points et conventions de points pleins ou vides).
Aucun corrigé officiel n'existe : tous les corrigés sont rédigés et chaque valeur numérique a été recalculée par script (sympy).

Le sujet n'imprime aucun total par question ni pour l'épreuve ; les points imprimés par bloc ((i), (ii)...) sont recopiés tels quels (leur somme est 103). Quand un même total couvre plusieurs sous-questions (ex. « (9 marks) » pour (a) et (b)), il est porté par la dernière sous-question du bloc, les autres ont `points` null, et `points` de chaque exercice est laissé vide.

Scan de 3 pages (page de garde + 2 pages de questions) : les questions 1 à 10 sont complètes et se suivent, aucune page ne semble manquer. L'étiquette en haut à gauche de la page de garde dit « Pure Maths With Stats 2 », en accord avec le cadre (Pure Mathematics With Statistics, Paper 2, code 0770) et le pied de page 00/0770/2.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The function $f$ is periodic with period $4$. Given that
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2 - 2 & \text{for } 0 \le x < 2, \\ 4 - x & \text{for } 2 \le x \le 4, \end{cases}$$
evaluate $f(19)$ and $f(-43)$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Since $f$ has period $4$, $f(x + 4k) = f(x)$ for every integer $k$. Reduce each argument into the interval $[0, 4)$.

**$f(19)$.** $19 = 4 \times 4 + 3$, so $f(19) = f(3)$. As $2 \le 3 < 4$, the second branch applies: $f(3) = 4 - 3 = 1$.

**$f(-43)$.** $-43 = 4 \times (-11) + 1$ (that is, $-43 + 44 = 1$), so $f(-43) = f(1)$. As $0 \le 1 < 2$, the first branch applies: $f(1) = 1^2 - 2 = -1$.

$$\boxed{f(19) = 1, \qquad f(-43) = -1}$$

Remark on the definition: at $x = 4$ the printed second branch would give $4 - 4 = 0$, but periodicity forces $f(4) = f(0) = 0^2 - 2 = -2$. The two requirements are incompatible at the single point $x = 4$, so the branch $4 - x$ is used on $2 \le x < 4$ only. This does not affect the two values above.

questions.enonce_markdown: Sketch the graph of $f(x)$ in the range $-4 \le x < 8$. (6 marks for part (i), (a) and (b) together)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**One period, $0 \le x < 4$.**
- On $0 \le x < 2$: $f(x) = x^2 - 2$, a parabola arc from $(0, -2)$ through $(1, -1)$ and the $x$-intercept $(\sqrt2, 0)$ up to $(2, 2)$.
- On $2 \le x < 4$: $f(x) = 4 - x$, a straight line segment from $(2, 2)$ down towards $(4, 0)$ (open circle at $(4, 0)$, because $f(4) = f(0) = -2$).
- The two pieces join without a jump at $(2, 2)$ since $2^2 - 2 = 2 = 4 - 2$. There is a jump at $x = 4$ (from $0$ down to $-2$), so the graph is discontinuous at $x = 4k$.

**Whole range $-4 \le x < 8$.** Repeat this pattern every $4$ units (translate by $-4$ and by $+4$):

| Interval | Rule | Start | End |
|---|---|---|---|
| $-4 \le x < -2$ | $(x + 4)^2 - 2$ | $(-4, -2)$ filled | $(-2, 2)$ |
| $-2 \le x < 0$ | $-x$ | $(-2, 2)$ filled | $(0, 0)$ open |
| $0 \le x < 2$ | $x^2 - 2$ | $(0, -2)$ filled | $(2, 2)$ |
| $2 \le x < 4$ | $4 - x$ | $(2, 2)$ filled | $(4, 0)$ open |
| $4 \le x < 6$ | $(x - 4)^2 - 2$ | $(4, -2)$ filled | $(6, 2)$ |
| $6 \le x < 8$ | $8 - x$ | $(6, 2)$ filled | $(8, 0)$ open (not included, since $x < 8$) |

Key features of the sketch: maximum value $2$ at $x = -2, 2, 6$ (corners where a parabola arc meets a line segment); minimum value $-2$ at $x = -4, 0, 4$ (filled dots at the start of each period, just after each downward jump); $x$-intercepts at $x = -4 + \sqrt2 \approx -2.59$, $\sqrt2 \approx 1.41$ and $4 + \sqrt2 \approx 5.41$ only (the line segments reach the axis only at the open endpoints $x = 0, 4$, where $f = -2$ instead); the graph crosses the $y$-axis at $(0, -2)$.

questions.enonce_markdown: A relation $\mathcal{R}$ is defined on $\mathbb{Z}$, the set of integers, by $a\mathcal{R}b$ if and only if $(a + b)$ is even. Show that $\mathcal{R}$ is an equivalence relation. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A relation is an equivalence relation if it is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. Let $a, b, c \in \mathbb{Z}$.

**Reflexive.** $a + a = 2a$ is even for every integer $a$, so $a\mathcal{R}a$.

**Symmetric.** Suppose $a\mathcal{R}b$, i.e. $a + b$ is even. Since $b + a = a + b$, $b + a$ is even too, so $b\mathcal{R}a$.

**Transitive.** Suppose $a\mathcal{R}b$ and $b\mathcal{R}c$, i.e. $a + b$ and $b + c$ are both even. Then
$$a + c = (a + b) + (b + c) - 2b.$$
This is a sum of two even numbers minus the even number $2b$, hence even. So $a\mathcal{R}c$.

$\mathcal{R}$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, therefore it is an equivalence relation on $\mathbb{Z}$. $\blacksquare$

(Its equivalence classes are the set of even integers and the set of odd integers: $a\mathcal{R}b$ exactly when $a$ and $b$ have the same parity.)
